fields.h1: Build Abandoned Cart Automation That Knows When to Stop
fields.hero_description: Build abandoned cart automation that sends each reminder on your timing and logs every cart in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Around a Left Cart
fields.features_subheading: Each part handles one decision about a cart, and every decision is saved to that cart's record.
fields.feature_1:
Carts and orders read from your store

The app connects to your store through its API and pulls each cart with its items, value, and contact details. It pulls new orders too, to match each order to its cart.
fields.feature_2:
Reminders on the schedule you write

You set the wait before each reminder and how many go out. Before every send, the app looks for a matching order, and a cart that became an order gets no more messages.
fields.feature_3:
Consent read before any message

Each shopper's saved consent picks the channel. Agreed to texts means an SMS, agreed to email means an email, and a cart with neither is logged and gets no message at all.
fields.feature_4:
Big carts handed to a sales rep

Pick a cart value where a person should step in. Carts above it skip the email sequence, and the rep you name is sent a direct message with the items and the buyer's contact.
fields.feature_5:
Orders counted per reminder

A dashboard shows carts left, reminders sent, and orders placed after each reminder, week by week. Read it to see whether the second or the third message earns its place.
fields.feature_6:
Your carts, in a database you own

Every cart, message, and order match is stored in a database you own, and nothing caps the tasks it runs. On paid plans you can export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: Where a Left Cart Goes Next
fields.tab_content_1:
Ordered by 1:40 PM, no 24-hour email

Odalys Fenwick leaves 2 tins of oolong worth $46 in her Ashgrove Tea cart at 9:10 AM. The app waits 1 hour and emails the first reminder at 10:10 AM. She places the order at 1:40 PM, the app matches it to cart #5520, and the 24-hour reminder is canceled. Each step is written to the cart's log.
fields.tab_content_2:
Texts go only to shoppers who said yes to texts

Brackenridge Candles saves each contact's consent, and the app reads it before a reminder. This morning 3 carts were left. Tobiah Lusk said yes to texts and gets an SMS. Marisol Quennell agreed to email only and gets an email. Henrike Dahlgaard gave no marketing consent: her cart is logged, and no message goes out.
fields.tab_content_3:
A $2,340 cart goes to a person, not an inbox

Copperleaf Furniture draws the line at $1,500. A $2,340 cart holding a walnut dining table is over it and skips the email sequence. Ruairi Okonjo on sales gets a direct message listing the cart's items and the buyer's phone number, and the cart stays open in his queue until he marks the call done.
fields.tab_content_4:
15 of 27 orders came after the first email

Every Monday at 8:00 AM, Hollowmere Pet Supply gets a report on last week's carts. Shoppers left 180 carts: 132 got a reminder email, and 48 had no contact details or consent. Of the 27 orders that followed a reminder, 15 came after the first email, 9 after the second, and 3 after the third.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Abandoned Cart Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set the rules for abandoned cart automation, test them on real carts, and then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 List the store events to read
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what counts as abandoned before anything else: a cart with at least one item, a saved email or phone number, and no order after a set wait. Write the wait in minutes, and leave out carts from your own staff and test accounts.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List the store events the app will read, at minimum a new cart and a placed order. Note the field that links an order to its cart, such as the cart ID or the shopper's email, because every stop rule depends on that match.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the schedule as a short table: how long each reminder waits and which channel it uses. Add the stop rules next to it: an order or an unsubscribe ends the sequence for that cart.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Record which consent each contact gave and the form it came from, then map each answer to a channel. Decide how a shopper takes consent back, and make that answer update the same field the app reads.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the cart value where a sales rep takes over, and name the rep. Decide whether a discount code appears at all, which reminder carries it, and how long the code stays valid.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run the rules on last month's carts
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run the rules against last month's carts before you switch anything on. Check how many reminders each shopper would have received, and look for any cart that would have been reminded after its order was placed.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it with Emergent and start small
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the rules and the report in one prompt, and Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard. Turn it on for email carts first, read the Monday report for two weeks, then add texts.

faq_plan.a: Abandoned cart automation is a workflow that follows up when a shopper adds products to an online cart and leaves without completing the purchase. It can send a reminder by email or text, hand the cart to a person, or stay quiet when the shopper has already ordered. The rules you write decide what counts as abandoned, how long to wait, and when the follow-up stops.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up abandoned cart automation?
faq_plan.a: Connect your store, define what counts as an abandoned cart, write the reminder schedule with its stop rules, and test it on past carts before going live. With Emergent's AI automation builder, you describe those rules in plain English, and Emergent builds the app along with its database and dashboard. The app pulls carts and orders with your store's API.

faq_plan.q: How long should abandoned cart automation wait before the first reminder?
faq_plan.hint: How to set up abandoned cart automation in send grid?
faq_plan.a: Start with 1 hour, then test it against your own carts. Send the first reminder at 1 hour for half of your abandoned carts and at 4 hours for the other half, for two weeks. Keep the wait that brings more orders per reminder sent, and run the same test on the gap before the second reminder.

faq_plan.q: Should abandoned cart automation send high-value carts to a salesperson?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the cart is worth a rep's call. Set the line from your own order history: find the carts that only turned into orders after a call or a chat, and start a little below their value. Have the reminder email go out anyway if the rep logs no call within a day. If the rep turns the cart into a formal quote, proposal automation can draft and track it.

faq_plan.q: Can abandoned cart automation reach a guest shopper who never signed in?
faq_plan.a: Only if the guest typed an email or phone number before leaving. A guest cart with no contact can be counted but not reminded. Ask for the email on the first checkout screen, before shipping and payment, and check whether your store's API returns the contact at that step. Emergent builds the app on a database you own, which stores every guest cart.

faq_plan.q: Should abandoned cart automation put a discount code in the email?
faq_plan.a: Not in the first reminder. Keep a code for the last message in the sequence, make it single-use, and set a short expiry such as 72 hours. Shoppers who would have finished anyway then pay full price. Count the orders that used the code on their own line in your report to see what the discount cost you.

faq_plan.q: Should abandoned cart automation pause my regular marketing emails?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for the few days the cart sequence runs. Hold the shopper's scheduled promotions until the sequence ends or they order. Each message they get then has one job. Give your newsletter automation a rule that skips any contact with an open cart sequence, and let them back into the next send once the cart closes.

faq_plan.q: How do I measure whether my abandoned cart automation is working?
faq_plan.a: Compare against a holdout group. Leave 1 in 10 abandoned carts with no reminder for a month, then compare orders per cart between the two groups: the difference is what the reminders added. A plain count of orders after a reminder can overstate it, since some shoppers come back on their own. Emergent can build the live dashboard that shows both groups side by side.

faq_plan.q: Can abandoned cart automation show the products still in the cart?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in the app Emergent builds. The app reads the cart's line items through your store's API and can place each product's name and price in the message. Check stock just before each send and leave out any item that has sold out. A reminder should not point to something the shopper cannot buy. Link the message to the saved cart, not the home page.

faq_plan.q: How should abandoned cart automation treat buyers who need approval?
faq_plan.a: Send the cart as a quote the buyer can forward, and pause reminders while it sits with their approver. Ask at checkout whether the order needs approval. If it does, email a quote with the cart's prices and an expiry date in place of the usual reminders, and use pdf automation to produce that quote from the cart. Follow up once, two days before the quote expires.

plan.angle: The top 10 are help-center setup guides for one email tool each and a vendor blog of best practices. This page shows the app a store owner builds around their own cart data: reminders that stop the moment an order lands, a consent check that picks text or email for each shopper, a handoff of big carts to a sales rep, and a Monday report of which reminder each order followed. The FAQ covers timing, guest carts, discount codes, newsletter overlap, measurement and business buyers as plain advice, with no recovery-rate statistics and no legal claims.
